← SOLSTICE PROJECT NOTES

Same-part-number GM pan family — visual topology evidence

Accessed and retained: 2026-10-13. This source adds visual context for the cast pan and factory baffle/pickup relationship; it adds no dimensional input to the Solstice model.

Evidence and scope

The 2008 Saturn Vue FWD service-manual reproduction includes a pan-casting inspection view and a separate “oil pan assembly” illustration. A 2008 Vue parts-list reproduction identifies pan 12601240 and baffle 12578196 for the 2.2/2.4 L applications. The Solstice LNF EPC already identifies the same pan and baffle numbers. This matching part identity makes the Vue drawings a useful same-part-number topology reference, while the Vue installation orientation and surrounding vehicle interfaces remain application-specific.

The service drawings visibly distinguish the cast pan, removable baffle scraper, its screw, the suction-pipe assembly, its strainer and separate pipe fasteners. The inspection image also shows a nonrectangular cavity, flange, cast ribs and bosses. These observations can guide labels and qualitative comparison in the display model; exploded spacing, linework and perspective are schematic.

Retained source files

The originals are kept under pan-family-illustrations/ with source URLs, byte lengths and SHA-256 values in manifest.json:

  • Pan-casting inspection view, from the 2008 Vue service-manual reproduction.
  • Oil-pan assembly view, from the same service-manual reproduction.
  • Baffle-scraper inspection view, from the same service-manual reproduction.
  • Vue oil-pan catalog reproduction, listing the matching pan and baffle identities.

The manual and parts list are third-party reproductions, not hosted by GM. The GM-hosted 12601240 product page independently confirms the published overall envelope and says the pan includes the pickup; it does not publish the illustrated hidden-cavity dimensions. The product page's fitment listing is not evidence that a Vue vehicle assembly is interchangeable with a Solstice assembly.

Model decisions

  • Do not scale these drawings, estimate boss coordinates from their pixels, or transfer Vue orientation to the Kappa chassis.
  • Keep the exterior GM envelope as the only source-backed pan dimensions. Keep cavity, cover, pickup path, floor, ribs, seats and placement as labeled proxy geometry.
  • Use the drawings to review whether the pan proxy's topology is plausible and to identify future component relationships; do not add metric ribs, bosses or holes without a source datum.
  • The current CAD solids and cut profiles were not changed by this evidence capture.

Related digital path finding

The current model now checks a sampled vertical withdrawal with the cover removed, both with the pickup/tube proxy retained and with that complete proxy assembly absent. In the nominal proxy, A/B/C collide with the rising tube after 7 mm of lift; the proxy-only vertical path clears when the pickup/tube assembly is omitted. This is a digital assembly-sequence hypothesis, not a verified Solstice service instruction. See the scenario assessment for every context and the exact tested limits.
